p: Additional documentary material
Closes the record of the correspondence

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Author’s page — C. W. Leadbeater, theosophical clairvoyant and writer.
p: Leadbeater was the leading clairvoyant investigator of the Adyar Society

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Explains the basis of the book: direct clairvoyant observation of the subtler bodies, and the conditions under which such observation is reliable.
p: The book rests on clairvoyant investigation
Observations are checked and cross-verified
The trained faculty, not fancy, is the instrument

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Maps the planes of nature — physical, astral, mental, and higher — as interpenetrating worlds of finer matter in which man simultaneously exists.
p: The planes interpenetrate like worlds within worlds
Each plane has its own order of matter
Man has a body appropriate to every plane

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Describes the clairvoyant faculty itself: what it sees, how it is developed, and its different grades.
p: Clairvoyance is an extension of normal sight
Its grades range from astral to buddhic vision
Development requires purity and training

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Surveys man’s vehicles — physical, astral, mental, causal — the bodies through which the one self works on each plane.
p: Each vehicle is built of the matter of its plane
The self works through all of them at once
The health of each body affects the others

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Presents the human trinity — spirit, intuition (buddhi), and intellect — the immortal triad that persists through incarnation.
p: The immortal triad is atma-buddhi-manas
It is the real man, the reincarnating ego
The personality is its temporary mask

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Describes the first and second life-outpourings from the logos, by which the matter of the planes is prepared and elemental essence is evolved.
p: The first outpouring ensouls the matter of the planes
The second builds the kingdoms of forms
Elemental essence is the raw material of desire and thought

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Explains the group-soul: how animals share a collective soul which gradually individualizes until a human ego is born.
p: Animals below the higher types share a group-soul
Individualization separates the human ego from the group
Domestic animals stand nearest the threshold

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Traces the upward curve of evolution from the mineral through plant and animal to man — the rising arc of returning spirit.
p: Evolution moves on a descending and ascending arc
Each kingdom prepares the next
Man stands on the ascending arc

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Describes human consciousness in its vehicles: how the ego works through the mental, astral, and physical bodies, waking and sleeping.
p: Consciousness functions on several planes at once
Sleep withdraws the ego into the astral and mental bodies
Dreams are the blurred record of astral life

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Describes the third outpouring — the descent of the divine spark that makes man a self-conscious soul, building the causal body.
p: The third outpouring creates the human ego
The causal body is its permanent vehicle
This is the true origin of the human soul

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Explains the mechanism of human evolution: experience gathered by the personality, transmuted into faculty by the ego, life after life.
p: Experience is transmuted into faculty
The ego grows by what it assimilates
Evolution is slow but unfailing

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Shows how the colours, forms, and textures of the invisible bodies reveal a man’s character, development, and temporary moods.
p: The aura is a mirror of character
Colours indicate quality; form indicates development
Every emotion leaves its visible trace

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Gives the key to the colours of the aura — what each hue signifies, from the crimson of anger to the pale blue of devotion and the gold of intellect.
p: Each emotion and quality has its characteristic colour
Spirituality shows as clear blue, violet, and gold
Muddy colours mean mingled or selfish motives

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Depicts the aura of the undeveloped man — coarse colours, irregular form — and how it changes as evolution proceeds.
p: The undeveloped aura is coarse and dull
Growth refines the colours and organizes the form
Self-control is visible as order in the aura

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Describes the astral and mental bodies of the ordinary cultured person — the mingled colours of an average character.
p: The ordinary aura is a mixture of good and ill
Every mood alters it temporarily
Permanent qualities show as stable bands of colour

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Illustrates the effect of sudden emotions — anger, fear, affection — as explosive changes in the aura, with the celebrated plates.
p: Sudden anger shows as vivid red flashes
Fear appears as a ghastly grey mist
Pure affection glows in clear rose

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Shows lasting states of character — devotion, intellect, irritability, melancholy — as permanent modifications of the aura.
p: Permanent traits shape the aura’s lasting texture
Devotion builds a soaring blue dome
Depression wraps the man in grey

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Describes the splendid aura of the spiritually developed man — luminous, ordered, radiant with the higher colours.
p: The developed aura is vast, clear, and luminous
Higher qualities add colours unseen in ordinary men
Such an aura blesses all who come within it

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Describes the health-aura — the radiance of vitality from the physical body — and its relation to health, disease, and magnetism.
p: Vitality radiates from the body as the health-aura
It absorbs and expels influences constantly
Magnetic healing works largely through it

title: Man Visible and Invisible
author: C. W. Leadbeater
chapter: 20. The Causal Body Of The Adept
s: Concludes with the causal body of the adept — the perfected vehicle of the master, glorious beyond description.
p: The adept’s causal body is a sphere of living light
It contains the harvest of countless lives
This is the goal toward which humanity evolves

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
s: Russell E. DiCarlo introduces Tolle as a teacher who points beyond words to a direct experience of Being. He frames the book as a living transmission: read slowly, and let the gaps between the words do the work.
p: The book is a pointer, not a doctrine — the truth it names is beyond words
Enlightenment is not a future attainment but a recognition of what is already here
Read with a feeling-awareness; pause when something resonates

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
s: Tolle tells his own story: years of anxiety and suicidal depression culminating in a night of inner dissolution — 'I cannot live with myself any longer' — that revealed the distinction between the false mind-made self and the deeper 'I'. He explains the book's question-and-answer origin and its purpose: to awaken readers to presence.
p: His crisis at 29 dissolved the unhappy self and left a deep peace
The 'I' and the 'self I cannot live with' exposed the split between Being and the egoic mind
The book arose from questions asked by students, clients, and friends
Markers like ¤ invite pauses to absorb rather than merely read

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
s: The first chapter names the core problem: identification with thinking. The voice in the head pretends to be you, but you are the awareness behind it. Enlightenment is simply the state of felt oneness with Being — found by watching the thinker, creating gaps of no-mind, and feeling the inner energy field of the body.
p: 'You are not your mind' — the observer of thought is who you really are
Enlightenment is your natural state of felt oneness with Being, not a superhuman feat
Watching the thinker and listening to the voice in the head begins disidentification
Gaps in thinking — even seconds of no-mind — are tastes of presence and peace

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
chapter: Consciousness: The Way Out of Pain
s: Tolle explains emotional pain as the pain-body: an accumulated residue of past suffering that lives in you and periodically feeds on negativity. The way out is not analysis but presence — watching the pain-body without judgment or identification, which cuts its food supply and transmutes it into consciousness.
p: The pain-body is a semi-autonomous energy form of old emotional pain
It awakens when triggered and seeks more pain to feed on
Witnessing it without identifying breaks the link and begins transmutation
Fear, guilt, anxiety and depression are ego-patterns sustained by unconsciousness

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
s: This chapter dismantles the illusion of psychological time. The past and future have no reality of their own; only the Now exists. Problems are mind-made projections into time, so 'there are no problems in the Now' — only situations to be dealt with or accepted. Presence dissolves the burden of time.
p: Nothing ever happened in the past or will happen in the future — it happens Now
Psychological time (endless past/future thinking) is the disease; clock time is a tool
Life's situations are handled in the Now; 'problems' are mind-stories about time
The quality of your consciousness now determines the future

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
chapter: Mind Strategies for Avoiding the Now
s: The mind resists the Now through ordinary unconsciousness (background unease) and deep unconsciousness (acute suffering). Waiting, complaining, blaming and impatience are all escape strategies. Tolle urges self-observation: catch the resistance, feel the negativity, and let presence burn it up.
p: Ordinary unconsciousness is the chronic low-level unease most people call normal
Waiting — for success, salvation, the future — is a core denial of the Now
Negativity is never the right response; it signals resistance to what is
Ask 'what is my relationship with the present moment?' to expose the mind's games

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
s: Presence is described in positive terms: deep alertness, stillness, and the felt sense of Being. Tolle compares it to waiting at the door of the senses, and to the alertness of a cat watching a mouse hole. Christ, Buddha, and the 'I Am' point to the same timeless state.
p: Presence is intense aliveness without thought — the state of 'no-mind' with eyes open
Sages have always pointed to it: the Kingdom, Nirvana, the Eternal Now
Presence is not a trance; it is hyper-alert, spacious stillness
You cannot think your way into presence — you feel your way in

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
s: The inner body is the practical doorway into presence. Feeling the subtle energy field within the body anchors attention in the Now, because the body is always present. Tolle gives practices: feeling the hands, following the breath, sensing the whole body from within — and explains forgiveness and slowing ageing as by-products.
p: The body cannot be in the past or future — feeling it pulls you into the Now
Sensing the inner energy field (hands, feet, whole body) is a direct portal
Forgiveness is reclaiming the present; holding grievances anchors you in time
Deep body awareness strengthens immunity and can slow ageing

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
s: Beyond form lies the Unmanifest — the formless source Tolle equates with Being, God, or the void. He surveys the doorways: the inner body, the dissolution of the world in death, the space between thoughts, silence, and dreamless sleep. Each portal is an opening to the eternal Now.
p: The Unmanifest is the invisible source of all form, not nothingness
Portals include inner body, gaps between thoughts, silence, sleep, and death
Space and silence are doorways because form needs both to exist
Death is not the opposite of life but the Unmanifest becoming visible

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
s: Tolle applies presence to intimacy. Relationships intensify both pain and awakening; love/hate cycles come from the pain-body and ego. A relationship becomes enlightened when partners stop making each other the source of happiness, allow each other to be, and use conflict as a mirror for consciousness.
p: Romantic love often masks dependency and pain-body attraction
Stop demanding your partner make you happy; take responsibility for your state
Presence transforms relating: acceptance, non-judgment, and space heal the bond
You do not need a partner to awaken — and aloneness can itself be a doorway

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
chapter: Beyond Happiness and Unhappiness There Is Peace
s: This chapter distinguishes happiness (which depends on conditions) from the deep peace of Being. It teaches acceptance of the present moment, the impermanence of all forms, the cyclical nature of life, and compassion that sees through ego drama without being pulled in.
p: Happiness depends on what happens; peace is untouched by conditions
Accept — then act. Non-resistance comes before effective action
Everything arises and passes; identifying with form guarantees suffering
Compassion is recognizing others' drama as pain-body and ego, not attacking it

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
s: The final chapter defines surrender not as weakness or resignation but as yielding to the flow of life — inner acceptance of what is, while acting powerfully from presence. It covers surrender in relationships, illness, disaster and suffering, the way of the cross, and the power to choose the Now.
p: Surrender is inner acceptance of this moment, not defeat or inaction
Nonresistance does not mean doing nothing — it means acting from presence, not reactivity
Illness and disaster can become portals: surrendered suffering opens into peace
There is only one choice to make: the Now — everything else follows

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: The author states the aim of The Secret Doctrine: to show that nature is not a fortuitous concurrence of atoms, to assign to man his rightful place in the universe, to rescue archaic truths, and to uncover the unity of all religions.
p: Nature is guided by intelligence, not chance
Archaic doctrine underlies all world religions
The book is a vindication of the ancient wisdom

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Preface To The Third And Revised Edition
s: Notes for the revised edition, prepared after the author’s death, recording the editorial care taken with the text.
p: The third edition preserves the original text
Editorial work done under the instructions she left

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Introduces the archaic manuscript from which the work is drawn, the existence of a secret record of human and cosmic evolution, and the grounds for believing in an unbroken esoteric tradition.
p: An archaic record of evolution exists
There is one unbroken esoteric tradition behind religions
The public is offered proofs, not asked for blind faith

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Proem: Pages From A Pre-Historic Record
s: The proem presents pages from the Book of Dzyan — the oldest record of cosmogenesis — and explains the method of commentary used throughout the work.
p: The Book of Dzyan is the archaic source-text
The stanzas describe the dawn of manifestation
Commentary is needed because the language is symbolic

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Seven Stanzas From The “Book Of Dzyan,” With Commentaries
s: The seven stanzas themselves: from the eternal darkness before manifestation, through the awakening of the logos, to the birth of the universe and the builders of the worlds.
p: Stanza I: the night of non-being before the dawn
The logos awakens and the word goes forth
The hierarchy of builders fashions the worlds

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Blavatsky’s detailed commentary on the stanzas: fohat, the divine breath, the lipikas, the seven elements, and the stages by which the cosmos comes into being.
p: Fohat is the dynamic energy of the logos
The lipikas are the agents of karmic law in cosmos
Manifestation proceeds from the formless to the formed

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On symbols, ideographs, and the picture-writing of the ancients as carriers of esoteric meaning.
p: Ideographs preserve esoteric knowledge in compressed form
Numbers and geometrical glyphs are keys of the mystery-language

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section II. The Mystery Language and Its Keys
s: Describes the mystery-language of the initiates — its seven keys and how a single glyph may be read on many planes.
p: The mystery-language has seven keys of interpretation
One symbol applies to cosmos, man, and the gods alike
Initiates alone hold all the keys

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section III. Primordial Substance and Divine Thought
s: On primordial substance — the rootless root of matter — and divine thought as the fashioner of the universe.
p: Primordial substance underlies all forms of matter
Divine thought is the architect of manifestation
Matter and spirit are two poles of the one reality

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Traces the triad chaos–theos–kosmos through Greek and Eastern systems: the abyss, the spirit brooding over it, and the ordered world.
p: Chaos is the unmanifested deep
Theos is the informing spirit
Kosmos is the harmony born of the two

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section V. On the Hidden Deity, Its Symbols and Glyphs
s: On the hidden deity — the unknowable all — and the glyphs by which the ancients hinted at it: the circle, the point, the cross.
p: The hidden deity is beyond all predicates
The circle and the point are its primal glyphs
All later gods are its manifested aspects

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: The symbol of the mundane egg — the world-egg of every cosmogony — and its meaning for the birth of the universe.
p: The egg is the universal symbol of the cosmos in germ
From the egg the manifested world is hatched
Every mythology preserves the figure

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section VII. The Days and Nights of Brahmâ
s: Explains the vast cycles of manifestation and rest — the days and nights of Brahmâ — and the immense chronological figures of the Hindus.
p: A day of Brahmâ is a period of manifestation
A night is a period of rest (pralaya)
The figures are symbolic yet harmonize with vast time-spans

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section VIII. The Lotus, as a Universal Symbol
s: The lotus as a world-symbol: rooted in the mud, rising through water, blooming in air — the emblem of spirit’s unfoldment.
p: The lotus images the growth of cosmos and soul
It is sacred from Egypt to India
Its stages figure the planes of manifestation

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section IX. The Moon; Deus Lunus, Phœbe
s: On the moon in archaic doctrine: her occult relation to the earth, her role in generation, and the lunar gods.
p: The moon is the earth’s elder and occult parent
Lunar influence governs generation and psychic tides
The lunar gods veil deep physiological mysteries

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section X. Tree, Serpent, and Crocodile Worship
s: Interprets tree, serpent, and crocodile worship — the tree of life, the serpent of wisdom, and the dragon of the deep.
p: The tree figures the universe and man
The serpent is the emblem of wisdom and of cycles
Crocodile and dragon carry the same archaic meaning

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XI. Demon est Deus Inversus
s: “The demon is god inverted”: how the gods of one people became the devils of another, and the true meaning of the fallen angels.
p: Gods degenerate into demons as religions supplant each other
The fallen angels are divine rebels only in theology
Esoterically they are the architects of the material world

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XII. The Theogony of the Creative Gods
s: The generation and hierarchy of the creative gods — the dhyanis, elohim, and demiurgic hosts who build the worlds.
p: Creation is the work of hierarchies, not one being
Dhyani-chohans, elohim, and demiurges are the same host
Their septenary orders reflect the cosmic law

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: The seven creations of the Puranas and other scriptures — the successive productions of the elements, the senses, and the worlds.
p: The Puranic creations are stages of cosmic unfolding
They correspond to the evolution of the elements and senses
The seventh creation is that of man

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On the four (esoterically five) elements — earth, water, air, fire, and ether — as the manifested aspects of the one element.
p: The elements are states of the one substance
The fifth, ether/akasa, is the connecting medium
Each element has its occult properties and regents

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XV. On Kwan-Shi-Yin and Kwan-Yin
s: On Kwan-shi-yin and Kwan-yin — the Chinese divine voices — and the parallels with the logos and the mystic sound.
p: Kwan-yin embodies the mystic sound, the voice of the silence
Parallels the logos doctrine of the West
The male and female aspects veil the same truth

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section I. Reasons for These Addenda
s: Explains why the addenda were added: to defend the archaic doctrines against the materialistic science of the time.
p: The addenda answer the objections of materialism
Science is invited to test the archaic claims

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section II. Modern Physicists are Playing at Blind Man’s Buff
s: Argues that physics gropes blindly because it ignores the ether and the intelligent forces behind phenomena.
p: Without the ether, physics cannot explain transmission
Forces are not dead pushes but intelligent agencies
Materialism mistakes effects for causes

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section III. Is Gravitation a Law?
s: Questions whether gravitation is a fundamental law, suggesting it is a mode of a deeper universal force — attraction and repulsion.
p: Gravitation is a mode, not an ultimate law
Attraction and repulsion are the two poles of one force
Occultism refers it to the life-currents of the cosmos

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section IV. The Theories of Rotation in Science
s: Criticizes scientific theories of planetary rotation and the nebular hypothesis from the occult standpoint.
p: The nebular hypothesis is questioned in its received form
Rotation is connected with the life of the planetary chain
Archaic astronomy knew more than it is credited with

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section V. The Masks of Science. Physics Or Metaphysics?
s: Shows that physics, pushed to its limits, becomes metaphysics — the masks of force and matter fall away.
p: The ultimate concepts of physics are metaphysical
Force and matter are veils of the one reality
Science unwittingly confirms the archaic teaching

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section VI. An Attack on the Scientific Theory of Force by a Man of Science
s: Cites a scientist’s own attack on the official theory of force, supporting the occult position.
p: Even orthodox science doubts its foundations
The criticism vindicates the esoteric view of force

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section VII. Life, Force, or Gravity
s: Discusses life, force, and gravity as modes of the one universal motion — the great breath of the cosmos.
p: All forces are modes of one universal motion
Life itself is a form of that motion
Gravity is its expression on the physical plane

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Examines the solar theory — the sun’s heat and constitution — and presents the occult view of the sun as a storehouse and reflector of the central spiritual sun.
p: The visible sun is the garment of a spiritual sun
Its heat is not what science supposed
The sun is the heart of the solar system, occultly

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section IX. The Coming Force. Its Possibilities And Impossibilities
s: On the “coming force” — the newly glimpsed powers of nature (with reference to Keely’s discoveries) — their promise and their dangers.
p: A new force of nature was on the point of discovery
Its misuse would be destructive
Only moral fitness can safely wield it

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section X. On the Elements and Atoms
s: On elements and atoms: the occult doctrine of the atom as a living, ensouled centre, against the dead billiard-ball atom of materialism.
p: The atom is a life, not a dead particle
Elements are phases of the one substance
Occult chemistry goes beyond the periodic table

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XI. Ancient Thought in Modern Dress
s: Shows modern scientific ideas arriving that are old occult teachings in modern dress.
p: Evolution, force-correlation, and ether are archaic ideas
The debt of science to the ancient wisdom is traced

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XII. Scientific and Esoteric Evidence for, and Objections to, the Modern Nebular Theory
s: Weighs the nebular theory in the balance of science and esotericism.
p: The theory is useful but partial
The esoteric account of world-formation differs fundamentally

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XIII. Forces—Modes of Motion or Intelligences?
s: Asks whether forces are mere modes of motion or the working of intelligences — and answers with the occult doctrine of the dhyanis.
p: Occultism sees intelligence behind every force
The dhyanis are the conscious agents of natural law
Blind force is the superstition of materialism

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XIV. Gods, Monads and Atoms
s: The summing chapter of the addenda: gods, monads, and atoms — the ladder of being from the atom to the archangel.
p: Every atom is a monad on the way to godhood
The ladder of being is unbroken
Life is one, in endless grades of self-expression

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XV. Cyclic Evolution and Karma
s: On cyclic evolution and karma: the law of periodic return and perfect justice that governs worlds and men.
p: Cycles govern all manifestation
Karma is the law of harmony restoring itself
Worlds, races, and souls all obey it

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XVI. The Zodiac and its Antiquity
s: On the zodiac, its immense antiquity, and its place as a record of archaic astronomy and a glyph of cosmic cycles.
p: The zodiac is a relic of the archaic science
Its signs veil the cycles of evolution
Its antiquity exceeds the guess of modern scholars

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XVII. Summary of the Position
s: Summarizes the whole volume: the reality of the archaic wisdom, the failure of materialism, and the promise of a spiritual science.
p: The archaic doctrine stands unrefuted
Materialism is a passing phase of thought
The future belongs to a synthesis of science and spirit

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. I
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: The author’s extensive notes, citations, and asides supporting the text.
p: Sources range across all ancient literatures
Many notes correct the errors of Orientalists of the day

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Editorial note prefacing the second volume.
p: Introduces the anthropogenesis volume

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Preliminary Notes on The Archaic Stanzas, and the Four Pre-Historic Continents
s: Preliminary notes on the archaic stanzas and the four pre-historic continents — the lands of the early root-races, including Lemuria and Atlantis.
p: Four great continents preceded ours
Each root-race had its own continental home
The stanzas record this forgotten history

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: The twelve stanzas of anthropogenesis: from the first ethereal race, through the sweat-born and egg-born races, to the separation of the sexes and the incarnation of the manasaputras.
p: The first race was ethereal and boneless
The races passed through sweat-born and egg-born stages
The sons of mind descended to awaken humanity

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Commentaries On The Twelve Stanzas And Their Terms, According To Their Numeration, In Stanzas And Shlokas
s: The great commentary on the anthropogenetic stanzas: the three-fold fall of the angels, the building of the physical form, the gift of mind, and the history of Lemuria and Atlantis.
p: The “fallen angels” are the mind-givers, the manasaputras
Physical man was built by the lunar ancestors
The sin of the mindless and the separation of the sexes are explained

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Concludes the anthropogenesis: the destiny of the races and the promise of the coming sixth race.
p: The fifth race has its work and its end
The sixth race is already in preparation
The cycle of humanity moves toward spirit again

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section I. Esoteric Tenets Corroborated in Every Scripture
s: Shows the esoteric tenets of the Secret Doctrine corroborated in the Bible, the Puranas, and every scripture.
p: The same doctrines recur in every scripture
Coincidences are too many for chance
The esoteric key makes them consistent

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On Adam-Adami: the generic man of Genesis read esoterically — not an individual but the race.
p: Adam is the race, not a person
The creation narrative is an allegory of the races
Esoteric reading removes the contradictions

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section III. The “Holy of Holies.” Its Degradation
s: On the Holy of Holies — the sacred mystery of generation — its original purity and its later degradation into phallic worship.
p: The creative mystery was originally reverenced as divine
Its symbols survive in every temple
Later ages degraded what the first ages held sacred

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section IV. On the Myth of the “Fallen Angels” in its Various Aspects
s: The myth of the fallen angels in its various aspects — the true history of the manasaputras who refused and those who incarnated.
p: The fall is the descent of the mind-givers into humanity
Those who “refused to create” and those who fell are distinguished
Satan is a theological inversion of a beneficent power

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section V. Is Plerôma Satan’s Lair?
s: A polemic against the theological identification of the pleroma — the gnostic fulness of the divine — with the realm of Satan.
p: The pleroma is the fulness of spiritual light
Theology has confounded it with darkness
Gnostic and Brahmanical parallels are drawn

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Prometheus the Titan — the Greek form of the mind-giver myth: the fire-bringer who suffered for man.
p: Prometheus is the Greek lucifer, the light-bringer
His gift of fire is the gift of mind
His chains are the chains of incarnation

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On Enoch and the Book of Enoch — the inner meaning of the antediluvian patriarch and his visions.
p: Enoch is a generic figure of the initiated seer
The Book of Enoch preserves fragments of the archaic doctrine
Its angels and watchers belong to the third race

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section VIII. The Symbolism of the Mystery-Names Iao and Jehovah, with their Relation to the Cross and Circle
s: The mystery-names Iao and Jehovah: their numerical and symbolic values, and their relation to the cross and the circle.
p: Divine names are numerical and geometrical ciphers
Iao and Jehovah veil the creative tetrad
The cross and circle are the oldest glyphs of the mystery

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section IX. The Upanishads in Gnostic Literature
s: Traces the doctrines of the Upanishads within gnostic literature — the identity of Indian and Alexandrian esotericism.
p: Gnosis and the Upanishads teach the same wisdom
The identity proves a common archaic source
Alexandria received what India preserved

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section X. The Cross and the Pythagorean Decad
s: On the cross and the Pythagorean decad — the sacred numbers and figures by which the ancients encoded the laws of evolution.
p: The decad is the perfect number of Pythagoras
The cross unfolds from the cube and encloses the man
Number is the key to nature’s harmonies

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XI. The Mysteries of the Hebdomad
s: The mysteries of the hebdomad — the sacred seven in planets, races, principles, and initiations.
p: Seven is the master-number of manifestation
The seven planets, races, and principles correspond
The hebdomad rules initiation and cosmos alike

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section I. Archaic, or Modern Anthropology?
s: Archaic versus modern anthropology: two accounts of man’s origin, and the grounds for preferring the former.
p: Modern anthropology builds on fragments
The archaic record is continuous and coherent
The two accounts are set side by side

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section II. The Ancestors Mankind is Offered by Science
s: Examines the ape-ancestry offered by science and rejects the descent of man from the anthropoid.
p: The ape is man’s descendant, not his ancestor — occultly
The missing link is not to be found in the bone-caves
Material resemblance is not parentage

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section III. The Fossil Relics of Man and the Anthropoid Ape
s: On the fossil relics of man and ape — what they prove and what they cannot prove.
p: Fossils are the record of the latest races only
The earliest races left no bones to find
Geological time is vaster than the science of the day allowed

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section IV. Duration of the Geological Periods, Race Cycles, and the Antiquity of Man
s: On the duration of geological periods and race-cycles — the enormous antiquity of man on earth.
p: Man’s antiquity runs into scores of millions of years
Race-cycles, not geological guesses, give the true measure
The figures of the secret science are stated

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section V. Organic Evolution and Creative Centres
s: On organic evolution and the creative centres — the inner, spiritual plan that guides the transformations of form.
p: Evolution works from within outward
Creative centres — the dhyanis — guide the building of forms
Blind selection is not the whole story

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section VI. Giants, Civilizations, and Submerged Continents Traced in History
s: Traces giants, lost civilizations, and submerged continents in the records of history and legend.
p: The giants of legend are the races of the early continents
Lemuria and Atlantis are historical, not mythical
Traditions of every people preserve the memory

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section VII. Scientific and Geological Proofs of the Existence of Several Submerged Continents
s: Gathers the scientific and geological proofs for the submerged continents — the evidence available to the nineteenth century.
p: Geology, botany, and zoology all bear witness
The distribution of species demands sunken lands
Science confirms what tradition preserved

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. II
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: The author’s notes and citations supporting the second volume.
p: Draws on geology, anthropology, and the world’s scriptures

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Preface explaining the origin and scope of the third volume — further esoteric instruction left by the author.
p: The volume gathers her later esoteric essays
It addresses the deeper doctrines only touched on before

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Introductory remarks on the state of theosophical teaching and the need for the papers here collected.
p: The papers answer questions left open by the first two volumes
They defend and extend the esoteric teaching

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: A preliminary survey of the field: the occult tradition, its custodians, and the misunderstandings it has met.
p: The occult tradition is one and continuous
Its custodians have always been few
Misunderstanding is the lot of every restatement

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section II. Modern Criticism and the Ancients
s: On modern criticism and the ancients — how scholarship misjudges the antiquity and meaning of the sacred books.
p: Modern criticism lacks the esoteric key
The ancients wrote for the initiated
Dates and authorships are wrongly assigned

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section III. The Origin of Magic
s: On the origin of magic — the remnant of the divine wisdom of the early races, degraded in later times.
p: Magic is the degenerated science of the fourth race
True magic was the spiritual knowledge of the initiates
Its modern form is a fallen shadow

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section IV. The Secrecy of Initiates
s: Why the initiates kept their knowledge secret — the law of silence and its reasons.
p: Secrecy guarded knowledge from the unready
Power without purity would destroy the world
The mysteries were veiled for humanity’s sake

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section V. Some Reasons for Secrecy
s: Further reasons for secrecy: the fate of premature disclosure and the duty of the custodians.
p: Premature disclosure has always brought ruin
The custodians answer for their trust
Silence is itself a protection

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section VI. The Dangers of Practical Magic
s: On the dangers of practical magic — psychic and spiritual — for the untrained and the selfish.
p: Practical magic multiplies the dangers of the path
Selfish motive turns it to sorcery
The unprepared operator risks body and soul

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section VII. Old Wine in New Bottles
s: Old wine in new bottles: the ancient wisdom reappearing in modern systems and movements.
p: Modern movements rediscover ancient truths
Theosophy presents the old wine without disguise

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section VIII. The Book of Enoch the Origin and the Foundation of Christianity
s: On the Book of Enoch as a fountain-head of Christian symbolism and doctrine.
p: The Book of Enoch underlies much of Christian imagery
Its angels and its messiah are archaic figures
Christianity drew from older wells than it admits

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section IX. Hermetic and Kabalistic Doctrines
s: On the Hermetic and Kabalistic doctrines — the Western form of the secret wisdom.
p: Hermeticism and the Kabalah are one stream with the East
Their glyph is the same: the unfolding of the one into the many

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section X. Various Occult Systems of Interpretations of Alphabets and Numerals
s: A survey of occult systems of alphabets and numerals — gematria, notaricon, and their kin.
p: Letters and numbers are ciphers of the doctrine
Each sacred alphabet encodes the cosmic process
The keys must be used with knowledge, not mechanically

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XI. The Hexagon with the Central Point, or the Seventh Key
s: The hexagon with the central point — the seventh key of the mystery-language and what it opens.
p: The seventh key unlocks the geometrical symbolism
The hexagram and the point figure the macrocosm and the microcosm
It is the key of keys for practical occultism

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XII. The Duty of the True Occultist toward Religions
s: The duty of the true occultist toward religions: to honour the spirit beneath every form while exposing corruption.
p: The occultist attacks superstition, not devotion
Every religion has a core of truth to be reverenced
Reform, not destruction, is the aim

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XIII. Post-Christian Adepts and their Doctrines
s: On the adepts who appeared after Christianity — the Rosicrucians and others — and their teachings.
p: The line of adepts did not end with antiquity
The Rosicrucians carried the torch in Europe
Their doctrines are the old wisdom under new names

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XIV. Simon and his Biographer Hippolytus
s: On Simon Magus and his biographer Hippolytus — the gnostic teaching of Simon and its misrepresentation.
p: Simon taught a pure gnostic system
His accusers have drawn the portrait we possess
The system is the archaic philosophy again

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XV. St. Paul the real Founder of present Christianity
s: St. Paul as the real founder of present Christianity — an initiate speaking in symbols the Church literalized.
p: Paul, not Jesus’ simple gospel, shaped the Church
His letters veil an initiate’s knowledge
Literalism has inverted his meaning

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XVI. Peter a Jewish Kabalist, not an Initiate
s: On Peter — a Jewish Kabalist, not an initiate of the higher mysteries — and the foundation of the Petrine Church.
p: Peter’s knowledge was exoteric Kabalism
The higher initiation is not his
The Church of Peter rests on a lower key

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On Apollonius of Tyana — the great pagan adept whose life parallels and surpasses the gospel wonders.
p: Apollonius was a true adept of the first century
His life shows the real meaning of the wonder-tales
History has dimmed what it could not deny

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XVIII. Facts underlying Adept Biographies
s: On the facts underlying the biographies of adepts — how legend grows around real men.
p: Adept biographies blend fact and symbol
The marvels have a basis in real powers
Discrimination is needed to read them

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XIX. St. Cyprian of Antioch
s: On St. Cyprian of Antioch — the magician turned saint — and what his legend preserves.
p: Cyprian’s legend preserves a memory of the mysteries
The magician-saint is a bridge between paganism and the Church

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XX. The Eastern Gupta Vidya and the Kabalah
s: Compares the Eastern gupta vidya (secret knowledge) with the Kabalah — two branches of one tree.
p: The Kabalah is the Western gupta vidya
Their correspondences prove a common source
Each preserves what the other has lost

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On the Hebrew allegories — the Pentateuch read as a book of symbols.
p: The Pentateuch is an allegorical book
Its patriarchs are races and its wonders are initiations
The literal reading is the veil

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXII. The “Zohar” on Creation and the Elohim
s: What the Zohar teaches on creation and the Elohim — the Kabalistic account beside the stanzas of Dzyan.
p: The Zohar’s creation parallels the stanzas
The Elohim are the creative host, not one god
Kabalistic and Eastern cosmogonies agree

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXIII. What the Occultists and Kabalists have to say
s: Gathers what occultists and kabalists have to say on the points at issue.
p: Testimonies of the two traditions are compared
Their agreement is the strength of the doctrine

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXIV. Modern Kabalists in Science and Occult Astronomy
s: On modern kabalists in science and the occult astronomy — the meeting of the new science with the old numbers.
p: Modern discoveries run on the old lines
Occult astronomy anticipates the telescopic age

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXV. Eastern and Western Occultism
s: Eastern and Western occultism — their unity and their difference of method.
p: The truth is one; the methods differ
The East meditates, the West experiments
Both roads lead to the same summit

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXVI. The Idols and the Teraphim
s: On idols and teraphim — the real meaning of image-worship and the animation of statues.
p: The idol was a focus, not a god
The teraphim had a real psychic use
Image-worship is degraded symbolism

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On Egyptian magic — the wisdom of the temples of Egypt and its rites.
p: Egyptian magic was the science of the sanctuary
Its rites were based on real knowledge of nature’s forces
The Book of the Dead is an initiatory text

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXVIII. The Origin of the Mysteries
s: On the origin of the mysteries — instituted by the adepts of the early races for the preservation of the doctrine.
p: The mysteries were founded by the initiates of the third and fourth races
They preserved the doctrine through the darkening ages
Every nation received a share

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXIX. The Trial of the Sun Initiate
s: The trial of the sun-initiate — the supreme ordeal of the Egyptian and other mysteries.
p: The final trial was undergone in the crypt or the pyramid
The candidate faced the symbols of death and rebirth
Successive degrees led to this consummation

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXX. The Mystery “Sun of Initiation”
s: On the mystic “sun of initiation” — the inner light that dawns at the great initiation.
p: The sun of initiation is the spiritual light within
Its rising is the new birth of the candidate
All sun-myths veil this interior fact

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXXI. The Objects of the Mysteries
s: The objects of the mysteries: instruction, purification, and the quickening of evolution for the fit.
p: The mysteries taught the unity of god, nature, and man
They purified and accelerated evolution
They were the universities of the ancient world

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXXII. Traces of the Mysteries
s: Traces of the mysteries in the rites, dramas, and symbols that survive.
p: Surviving rites are fragments of the mystery-drama
Masonry and church ritual alike preserve the traces
The myth of the dying god is the mystery-plot

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXXIII. The Last of the Mysteries in Europe
s: On the last of the mysteries in Europe — the closing of the schools and the driving of the doctrine underground.
p: The schools were closed by the rising Church
The doctrine survived in secret societies
The dark ages of Europe were the exile of the wisdom

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXXIV. The Post-Christian Successors to the Mysteries
s: The successors of the mysteries after Christianity: the gnostics, the alchemists, the Templars, the Rosicrucians.
p: A chain of secret bodies succeeded the mysteries
Alchemy and Rosicrucianism carried the inner teaching
Persecution proves the continuity

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXXV. Symbolism of Sun and Stars
s: On the symbolism of the sun and stars — the sidereal glyphs of the doctrine.
p: The sun is the glyph of the logos
The stars are the hieroglyphs of the powers
Astronomy was once a sacred science

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXXVI. Pagan Sidereal Worship, or Astrology
s: On pagan sidereal worship — astrology as the surviving fragment of a sacred science.
p: Astrology is the fallen remnant of a true science
The stars condition, they do not compel
The wise man rules his stars

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XXXVII. The Souls of the Stars—Universal Heliolatry
s: On the souls of the stars and the universality of sun-worship — every star a living being.
p: Every star is ensouled
Sun-worship is the natural religion of humanity
Heliolatry veils the doctrine of the solar logos

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Distinguishes astrology from astrolatry — the science from the superstition.
p: Astrolatry is worship; astrology is observation
The true science reads tendencies, not fates

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On cycles and avataras — the periodic descent of divine teachers at the turning of the ages.
p: A teacher appears at the close of every cycle
The avatara is the logos manifesting in a vehicle
The law of cycles governs the comings

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On the secret cycles — the hidden periods that govern races, religions, and the rise and fall of nations.
p: History moves in secret cycles
The rise and fall of nations obey them
The initiated know the times and seasons

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XLI. The Doctrine of Avataras
s: The doctrine of avataras examined in detail — the kinds of divine descent and their purpose.
p: Avataras are of many grades and kinds
The descent answers a cyclic need
Krishna and Buddha are the great examples

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On the seven principles of man — the complete septenary analysis restated and deepened.
p: Man is sevenfold: body to spirit
Each principle has its own life and fate
The doctrine is the key to after-death states

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XLIII. The Mystery of Buddha
s: The mystery of Buddha — his real doctrine, his esoteric school, and what he taught beyond the popular creed.
p: Buddha taught an esoteric doctrine to his arhats
The popular Buddhism is the exoteric shell
His silence on the absolute was itself a teaching

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On the “reincarnations” of Buddha — the doctrine of the living Buddhas and the tulku succession.
p: The Buddha-principle continues to manifest
The tulku doctrine preserves an occult fact
The succession is of office, not of personal soul

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XLV. An Unpublished Discourse of Buddha
s: An unpublished discourse of Buddha — a teaching preserved in the esoteric records.
p: The discourse expounds the middle way esoterically
It bridges the doctrines of self and non-self

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On nirvana and moksha — the true meaning of liberation, beyond annihilation and beyond heaven.
p: Nirvana is not annihilation but absolute being
Moksha is liberation from the wheel of births
The state transcends description

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XLVII. The Secret Books of “Lam-Rin” and Dzyan
s: On the secret books of the Lam-rim and Dzyan — the hidden texts of the Tibetan tradition from which the stanzas were drawn.
p: The Book of Dzyan is the fountainhead of the stanzas
The Lam-rim is the graded path of Tibetan esotericism
The secret volumes are guarded in the trans-Himalayan schools

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section XLVIII. Amita Buddha Kwan-Shai-yin, and Kwan-yin.—What the “Book of Dzyan” and the Lamaseries of Tsong-Kha-pa say
s: On Amitabha, Kwan-shi-yin, and Kwan-yin — what the Book of Dzyan and the lamaseries of Tsong-kha-pa say of these divine figures.
p: Amitabha is the boundless light, the celestial Buddha
Kwan-yin is the divine voice, the melodious heaven
These figures veil cosmic principles

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: On Tsong-kha-pa, the reformer of Tibetan Buddhism, and the lohans (arhats) in China.
p: Tsong-kha-pa purified and reformed the doctrine in Tibet
The lohans are the adepts of the Chinese tradition
His school guards the esoteric line

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section L. A few more Misconceptions Corrected
s: Corrects further misconceptions about theosophy, the Masters, and the doctrine.
p: Popular errors about the Masters are answered
The teaching is defended against misreading

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Section LI. The “Doctrine of the Eye” & the “Doctrine of the Heart,” or the “Heart’s Seal”
s: The doctrine of the eye versus the doctrine of the heart — the exoteric knowledge versus the esoteric compassion, and the “heart’s seal” of the true teaching.
p: The eye-doctrine is the head-learning of the schools
The heart-doctrine is the living wisdom of compassion
The heart’s seal marks the true transmission

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Some Papers On The Bearing Of Occult Philosophy On Life
s: A series of papers on the bearing of occult philosophy on daily life — practical applications of the doctrine.
p: The doctrine is meant to be lived
Its ethics transform conduct and motive
Practical papers on will, thought, and duty

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Appendix. Notes on Papers I., II. and III
s: Appendix notes to the foregoing papers.
p: Clarifications and additional references

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Notes on oral teachings received by the inner group — instruction given by the author to her esoteric students.
p: Oral instruction supplemented the published work
The notes preserve her last teaching

title: The Secret Doctrine — Vol. III
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Notes and references for the third volume.
p: Sources across Eastern and Western esoteric literature

title: The Shape of Things to Come — Topic Consolidation
author: H. G. Wells
s: An overview of the whole book’s structure — the five books of the future history and their periods.
p: The work is framed as Dr. Raven’s dream book
Five books carry the history from 1930 past 2105
Each book marks a phase of the world-state’s coming

title: The Shape of Things to Come — Topic Consolidation
author: H. G. Wells
chapter: Book Two: The Age of Frustration (1960-1978)
s: Book Two — the age of frustration at its depth: governmental failure, social disintegration, the final war cyclone, and biological warfare.
p: Governments fail; education revolutionizes first
The final wars devastate the old civilization
Out of breakdown comes the will to world order

title: The Shape of Things to Come — Topic Consolidation
author: H. G. Wells
s: Book Three — the world renascence: modern state planning, the revolutionary model, and the struggle to found the new order.
p: Planning replaces drift
A competent minority leads the reconstruction
Resistance is overcome by persistence and results

title: The Shape of Things to Come — Topic Consolidation
author: H. G. Wells
chapter: Book Four: The Modern State Militant (2059-2105)
s: Book Four — the modern state militant: the phase of enforcement and the cultural revolution that secures the world-state.
p: The world-state passes through a militant phase
Enforcement gives way to cultural consolidation

title: The Shape of Things to Come — Topic Consolidation
author: H. G. Wells
s: A review of the book’s key predictions and themes — what Wells foresaw rightly, what he missed, and his core arguments.
p: Some forecasts proved startlingly accurate
Others missed the mark
The core argument: world order or chaos

title: The Shape of Things to Come — Topic Consolidation
author: H. G. Wells
s: Notes on the consolidation document itself.
p: Describes the scope and method of the study companion

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Author’s page — Annie Besant, president of the Theosophical Society.
p: Besant led the Society from 1907 to 1933

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Besant explains the book’s purpose: a plain statement of the main theosophical teachings for students approaching the subject for the first time.
p: Written as a first textbook of theosophy
Based on lectures and earlier manuals

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Introduces the ancient wisdom as the one truth behind all religions, preserved by the great teachers and now restated for the modern world.
p: One wisdom underlies all religions
The great teachers are its guardians
Theosophy is its modern presentation

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Describes the physical plane — its seven subdivisions from solid to etheric — and man’s physical body with its etheric double.
p: The physical plane has seven sub-planes, including four ethers
The etheric double is the vehicle of vitality
Physical matter is the densest garment of spirit

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Describes the astral plane — the world of emotion and desire — its matter, its inhabitants, and the astral body in which man functions there.
p: The astral is the plane of feeling and desire
Astral matter responds instantly to emotion
The astral body is man’s vehicle of sensation

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Explains kâmaloka, the astral world entered after death, its regions, and the condition of the dead who pass through it.
p: Kâmaloka is the astral dwelling of the dead
Its regions range from dark to luminous
The dead remain until earthly desire is exhausted

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Describes the mental plane — the world of thought — its two great divisions (rûpa and arûpa), and the mental body and its powers.
p: The mental plane is the realm of thought
Its lower levels bear forms; its higher are formless
Thought here builds and acts directly

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Describes devachan, the heaven-world — the blissful mental-plane state where the soul assimilates the fruits of its past life between incarnations.
p: Devachan is the heaven-world of rest and assimilation
Each soul creates its heaven from its own highest aspirations
It is followed inevitably by return to birth

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Touches the planes beyond the mind: the buddhic plane of unity and compassion and the nirvânic plane of pure spirit.
p: The buddhic plane is the realm of unity and compassion
The nirvânic plane is the home of the spirit
On these planes separateness dissolves

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Presents reincarnation as the soul’s method of evolution — life after life in new bodies, gathering experience toward perfection.
p: The soul evolves through many lives
Each incarnation is a day in the soul’s school
Evolution’s slowness demands repeated birth

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Continues the argument: objections answered, the method of rebirth explained, and the justice of the law vindicated.
p: Objections from heredity and memory are answered
The ego chooses its conditions through past karma
Justice rules the succession of lives

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Expounds karma, the law of cause and effect on every plane — how thought, desire, and action weave destiny, and how knowledge makes man free within the law.
p: Karma is the law of causation applied morally
Thought is the mightiest force in making karma
Knowledge of the law is the beginning of freedom

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Reveals sacrifice as a cosmic law: the descent of spirit into matter, the logos limiting itself to give being, and man’s redemption through self-offering.
p: Sacrifice is the law of manifestation itself
The divine life limits itself to ensoul a world
Man fulfils the law by self-surrender and service

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Traces the stages of human ascent: the probationary path, initiation, and the rising grades of discipleship toward adeptship.
p: The path of ascent is marked by initiations
Discipleship has grades of increasing responsibility
Adeptship is the flower of human evolution

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Shows the vast context: how a solar system is built and guided by its logos and ministers, through chain, round, and race.
p: A solar system is the body of its logos
Worlds evolve through chains, rounds, and races
Man’s little life is set in a cosmic order

title: The Ancient Wisdom
author: Annie Besant
s: Notes and references supporting the text.
p: Draws on The Secret Doctrine and Eastern scriptures

title: The Divine Plan (Excerpt)
author: Geoffrey A. Barborka
s: Chapter IX opens the doctrine of the Rounds — the sevenfold pilgrimage of the life-wave around the planetary chain, each round repeating on a higher scale the work of the one before.
p: A round is one complete circuit of the life-wave around the chain
Each round repeats the former work on a higher scale
The doctrine is the key to the planetary evolution of man

title: The Divine Plan (Excerpt)
author: Geoffrey A. Barborka
chapter: The Relation of Rounds and Races
s: On the relation of rounds and races — how the seven root-races on one globe correspond to the greater cycle of the rounds.
p: Seven races on a globe mirror the seven rounds of the chain
The grand cycle includes mankind’s progress through all kingdoms
Race-evolution is the lesser wheel within the greater

title: The Divine Plan (Excerpt)
author: Geoffrey A. Barborka
chapter: The Relation of Rounds and Spheres
s: On the relation of rounds and spheres — the globes of the chain, the earth casting off her old skins, and the septenary spheres of being.
p: The chain’s globes are on different planes of being
The earth “casts off old skins” as the rounds proceed
Each globe has its place in the ladder of life

title: The Divine Plan (Excerpt)
author: Geoffrey A. Barborka
chapter: The Relation of Rounds and Watchers
s: On the relation of rounds and watchers — the great beings who watch successively over the rounds and races.
p: Watchers preside over the rounds in succession
The hierarchy of guardians is part of the plan
Human evolution is guided, not accidental

title: The Divine Plan (Excerpt)
author: Geoffrey A. Barborka
chapter: The Relation of Rounds and the After-Death States
s: On the relation of the rounds to the after-death states — the devachanic and kama-lokic conditions keyed to the greater cycles.
p: The after-death states belong to the same cyclic law
Man’s principles answer to the globes and rounds
Death and rebirth are small rounds within the great

title: The Divine Plan (Excerpt)
author: Geoffrey A. Barborka
chapter: The Relation of Rounds and Principles
s: On the relation of rounds and principles — how the seven principles of man correspond to the rounds, the higher principles awaiting the future rounds.
p: Each round develops one principle of the seven
The superior rounds will awaken the dormant principles
The fifth round will unfold the fifth principle fully

title: The Divine Plan (Excerpt)
author: Geoffrey A. Barborka
s: Chapter X on the after-death states — the conditions of the entity between lives, the sleep of the personality, and the destiny of the reincarnating ego.
p: The personality sleeps while the ego endures
The after-death journey has definite stages
Understanding death removes its terror

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Introductory: what occultism is — the study of the hidden side of things, the unseen forces and beings that surround and influence us.
p: Occultism studies the hidden side of nature
The unseen constantly influences the seen
The book is a survey of those influences

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: On the world as a whole — the solar system as a living being, its logos, and the planes of nature as fields of unseen activity.
p: The solar system is a living whole
Its logos is its life
The planes are the fields of the unseen work

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How we are influenced by the planets — the real basis of astrological influence as observed occultly.
p: Planetary influence is a fact of the inner world
Each planet pours its own magnetism
The wise use the tides; they are not ruled by them

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How we are influenced by the sun — physical vitality and the spiritual outpouring behind it.
p: The sun pours vitality as well as light
Behind the physical sun stands the spiritual sun
Sunlight is the great purifier on every plane

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How natural surroundings influence us — mountains, forests, sea; the magnetism of places.
p: Every landscape has its own magnetism
Forests, sea, and mountains differ in their influence
Sensitive people respond strongly to place

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How nature-spirits influence us — the fairy kingdom, its types, and its relations with man.
p: Nature-spirits are a real order of evolving life
They avoid or approach men by temperament
They are the agents behind much of nature’s beauty

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: On centres of magnetism — sacred places, shrines, and spots charged by devotion or event.
p: Places become charged by long devotion
Shrines radiate the influence stored in them
Battlefields and prisons hold darker charges

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How ceremonies influence us — the real inner effect of ritual, music, incense, and ordered worship.
p: Ceremony builds actual forms on the higher planes
Music and incense have definite inner effects
Collective worship creates a real reservoir of force

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How sounds influence us — music, mantra, and noise on the unseen planes.
p: Sound builds form on the subtler planes
Music can purify or degrade the atmosphere
Noise has a genuinely destructive effect

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How public opinion influences us — the pressure of collective thought-currents on the individual.
p: Public opinion is a real current of force
Individuals are bathed in it constantly
Independence of mind is an occult defence

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How occasional events — celebrations, disasters, elections — stir the inner atmosphere and influence all within it.
p: Great events leave an astral stir
Crowd emotion amplifies the effect
The student learns to stand aside

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How unseen beings — the dead, the nature-spirits, the devas, and darker entities — influence the living.
p: The dead remain near and can help or hinder
Devas bless; lower entities obsess
Knowledge removes the fear of the unseen

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Our right attitude toward all these influences — neither fear nor credulity, but knowledge and self-mastery.
p: Knowledge is the only sure defence
Fear opens the door; calmness closes it
Self-mastery makes one immune

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How we influence ourselves by our habits — the building of the bodies by repeated thought and act.
p: Habit is crystallized thought
The bodies are shaped by what we repeat
Good habits are the foundation of the inner life

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How we influence ourselves through physical environment — food, drink, clothing, cleanliness, and their unseen effects.
p: The physical body is the temple of the work
Diet and cleanliness have occult effects
Simplicity aids sensitivity

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How we influence ourselves by our mental conditions — the moods and thoughts that build our inner climate.
p: The mind creates its own weather
Cheerfulness is an occult virtue
Worry is a slow poison on every plane

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How we influence ourselves by our amusements — recreation, reading, and pleasure judged from the inner side.
p: Amusements build or debilitate the bodies
True recreation refreshes; dissipation corrodes
Choose pleasures that leave no stain

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How we influence others by what we are — character as a silent, ceaseless radiation.
p: What we are speaks louder than what we say
Character radiates whether we will or not
The greatest service is self-improvement

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How we influence others by what we think — thought-forms reaching those we think of.
p: Every thought of another reaches them
Thoughts of love protect; thoughts of harm attack
Think of others as you would heal them

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How we influence others by what we do — action and example on the seen and unseen planes.
p: Actions have invisible consequences
Example is the most powerful teaching
Right action purifies the shared atmosphere

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How we influence others by collective thought — class, nation, and the shared thought-forms of communities.
p: Groups think together, for good or ill
Prejudice is a collective thought-form
To think truly is to serve one’s nation

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: How we influence children — the plastic inner bodies of the young and the sacred responsibility of parent and teacher.
p: The child’s inner bodies are exquisitely plastic
Atmosphere teaches more than precept
To guard a child’s aura is a sacred trust

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
chapter: 23. By Our Relation To Lower Kingdoms
s: How we influence the lower kingdoms — animals, plants, and minerals — and our responsibility toward them.
p: Our treatment of animals hastens or retards their evolution
Kindness to the lower kingdoms is cosmic work
Cruelty has its karmic harvest

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: The results of this knowledge — what changes when a man knows the hidden side of things.
p: Knowledge brings responsibility
The occultist lives more carefully than other men
Every detail of life becomes significant

title: The Hidden Side of Things
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: The way to seership — how the faculty of seeing the hidden side may be safely developed.
p: Seership is the fruit of purity and training
There is no shortcut that is safe
The inner sight opens when the life is ready

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Author’s page — C. W. Leadbeater, presiding lecturer of the Adyar community.
p: The talks were originally given to resident students
