author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: A note on the Indian edition of these collected talks.
p: The talks were gathered for wider circulation

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Introduces the talks as informal instruction given to students living at the Theosophical Society’s headquarters at Adyar.
p: Talks delivered at Adyar to students
Aim: the inner side of theosophical life, not its literature

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
chapter: First Section: The Great Ones And The Way To Them
s: Talks on the Masters of the Wisdom — who they are, how they live and work, and the qualifications and path by which a pupil may approach them.
p: The Masters are living men of perfected development
The way to them lies through service and self-purification
The relationship of pupil and Master is described

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Talks on religion from the theosophical standpoint — the common core of the faiths, and worship, prayer, and ceremony as seen from the inner side.
p: All religions spring from one source
Ceremony and prayer have real inner effects
True religion is a life, not a creed

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: On the attitude theosophy asks of its students: tolerance, impersonality, discrimination, and the harmony of study with service.
p: Tolerance of all beliefs is fundamental
Impersonality frees one from petty reactions
Study must be balanced by service

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Descriptions of the higher planes of nature — the astral, mental, buddhic, and beyond — and man’s life and possibilities upon them.
p: The higher planes are states of subtler matter and consciousness
Man can learn to function consciously upon them
Each plane has its own inhabitants and laws

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
chapter: Fifth Section: The Ego And His Vehicles
s: On the ego — the real man — and his bodies: how the individuality builds, uses, and discards its vehicles life after life.
p: The ego is the enduring individuality
Its vehicles are temporary instruments
Growth is the ego’s gradual mastery of its bodies

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: A note introducing the talks to American readers.
p: The second series continues the Adyar talks

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Leadbeater’s note on the circumstances and purpose of the talks.
p: The talks were taken down by hearers and revised

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Talks on the conditions after death — kama-loka and devachan — the fate of various types of men, and how to help the dead.
p: Death is a change of state, not of self
After-death conditions follow the life’s dominant note
Thought and prayer can genuinely help the dead

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: On the work done on the astral plane by the living — during sleep — and by helpers of humanity, visible and invisible.
p: The living can work on the astral plane during sleep
Helpers assist the dead and the distressed
Such work is a natural extension of service

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
chapter: Third Section: The Mental Body And The Power Of Thought
s: On the mental body: its structure, its training, and the creative power of thought — thought-forms, their effects, and the duty of thought-control.
p: Thought is a creative force building actual forms
The mental body grows by exercise and purity of thought
We are responsible for our thought-currents

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: On psychic faculties — clairvoyance, clairaudience, and the rest — their nature, their place in evolution, and the right attitude toward them.
p: Psychic powers are latent in all men
They are by-products, not the goal, of the path
Safety lies in purity and guidance

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: On the deva (angelic) evolution and the nature-spirits — the other lines of life sharing our world.
p: The devas are a parallel line of evolution
Nature-spirits are the beings behind the forces of nature
Cooperation between the lines is part of the divine plan

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
chapter: Sixth Section: The Worlds And The Races Of Men
s: On the planetary scheme: the chain of worlds, the rounds, and the root-races through which humanity evolves.
p: Humanity evolves through successive root-races
Each race has its continent and its work
The planetary chain is the field of this vast growth

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Talks on reincarnation — its justice, its method, and its consolations.
p: Rebirth explains life’s inequalities
The interval between lives is part of the process
Knowledge of the law removes the fear of death

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: On karma — the working of the law of cause and effect in individual and collective life.
p: Karma adjusts all action with perfect justice
Nations as well as individuals have karma
Understanding karma teaches acceptance and effort

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
chapter: Ninth Section: The Theosophical Society And Its Founders
s: On the Theosophical Society — its founding by the Masters through H. P. Blavatsky, its mission, and the duties of its members.
p: The Society was founded under the Masters’ direction
H. P. Blavatsky was their chosen messenger
Loyalty to the Society’s objects is the member’s duty

title: The Inner Life
author: C. W. Leadbeater
s: Notes and references for the talks.
p: Sources include The Secret Doctrine and the Society’s history

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Blavatsky explains the purpose of the book: to answer, in plain question-and-answer form, the questions most often asked about Theosophy and the Theosophical Society.
p: Written as a dialogue between an enquirer and a theosophist
Intended as a clear, simple introduction for the public

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: I. Theosophy And The Theosophical Society
s: Defines Theosophy as divine wisdom — the esoteric truth behind all religions — and distinguishes it from the Theosophical Society, the modern body founded in 1875 to study and promote it.
p: Theosophy = the wisdom-religion underlying all faiths
The T.S. founded in New York, 1875
The Society is the vehicle, not the teaching itself

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Explains the difference between the Society’s public work and its inner, esoteric teaching, and outlines the Society’s three declared objects, including universal brotherhood.
p: Exoteric section open to all; esoteric teaching for pledged students
First object: universal brotherhood without distinction
Study of comparative religion and the latent powers of man

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: III. The Working System Of The T.S.
s: Describes how the Society is organized and governed, its sections, and the duties of members, stressing tolerance and non-interference with members’ beliefs.
p: The Society has no dogmas and no creed
Members may hold any religion or none
Organization exists to serve study and brotherhood

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: IV. The Relations Of The Theosophical Society To Theosophy
s: Clarifies that the Society does not invent or own Theosophy; it revives and presents ancient wisdom, drawing on Eastern scriptures and the teachings of the Masters.
p: Theosophy is archaic, not a new invention
The Society is a channel for the ancient wisdom
The Masters of Wisdom stand behind the movement

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: V. The Fundamental Teachings Of Theosophy
s: Introduces the core doctrines: the one absolute, unknowable principle; the universality of law; karma; reincarnation; and the septenary constitution of man and cosmos.
p: One absolute, infinite, unknowable principle
Law is universal — karma governs all planes
Man is a septenary being, mirroring the cosmos

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: VI. Theosophical Teachings As To Nature And Man
s: Sets out the theosophical view of nature as alive and ensouled, and of man as a compound being of body, soul, and spirit evolving through cycles.
p: Nature is living and ensouled at every level
Man is a triad: body, soul (mind), and spirit
Evolution proceeds through vast cosmic cycles

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: VII. On The Various Post Mortem States
s: Explains what happens after death: the separation of the principles, the astral shell, and the states of kama-loka and devachan experienced by the disembodied entity.
p: Death separates the lower principles from the higher triad
Kama-loka is the realm of purification from desire
Devachan is the blissful, dream-like state of assimilation

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Argues for reincarnation as the just and logical explanation of human inequality, genius, and moral growth, distinguishing it from transmigration into animals.
p: Rebirth explains inequality, genius, and justice
The true individuality reincarnates, not the personality
Theosophy rejects transmigration of the human soul into animals

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: IX. On The Kama-Loka And Devachan
s: Details the after-death journey: the astral body’s sojourn in kama-loka, the “second death”, and the devachanic rest where the soul assimilates the experiences of the life just ended.
p: Kama-loka corresponds to the earth’s astral atmosphere
The “second death” frees the ego from the desire-body
Devachan is subjective bliss proportioned to merit

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: X. On The Nature Of Our Thinking Principle
s: Discusses manas, the thinking principle, as the real human individuality — the link between the mortal personality and the immortal spirit.
p: Manas is the reincarnating ego, the thinker
Lower manas is entangled with desire; higher manas turns to spirit
Mind is the battlefield of the human evolution

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: XI. On The Mysteries Of Re-Incarnation
s: Answers difficult questions about rebirth: intervals between lives, memory of past lives, infant prodigies, and why we do not remember former incarnations.
p: The interval in devachan varies with the life’s spiritual quality
Memory of past lives resides in the individuality, not the brain
Genius and intuition are fruits of past-life effort

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Turns from doctrine to duty: practical theosophy means living the ethics — charity, tolerance, self-sacrifice — and working for humanity rather than chasing phenomena.
p: Duty, not phenomena, is the heart of practical theosophy
Charity and tolerance are the first duties of members
Occult powers are a distraction from the true path

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: XIII. On The Misconceptions About The Theosophical Society
s: Refutes common charges against the Society — that it is anti-Christian, a money-making scheme, or a political body — and explains its true non-sectarian character.
p: The Society is not anti-Christian but anti-dogmatic
It has no political aims or ambitions
Misrepresentations spring from prejudice and misunderstanding

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Describes the Mahatmas — living adepts of the East — their existence, their relation to the Society, and why they remain hidden from the profane world.
p: The Mahatmas are living men of great wisdom and holiness
They directed the founding of the Society
They work for humanity, not for public display

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Conclusion. The Future Of The Theosophical Society
s: Closes with a forecast of the Society’s mission: to keep the nucleus of universal brotherhood alive and to prepare the ground for the teachers of the coming century.
p: The Society’s future depends on fidelity to its first object
A new messenger is prophesied for the closing quarter of the 20th century
The work endures if the members remain true

title: The Key to Theosophy
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Notes and references supporting the dialogue, citing Eastern scriptures, scientists, and philosophers.
p: Sources range from the Upanishads to modern science
Clarifications of technical terms used in the text

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Author’s page — William Quan Judge, co-founder of the Theosophical Society.
p: Judge co-founded the T.S. with Blavatsky and Olcott in 1875

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Judge states his aim: to present the complete system of theosophy in brief, plain language for the general reader.
p: Written for the general reader, not the specialist
Attempts to cover the whole ocean of theosophy in a small compass

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Introduces the Masters of Wisdom — the adepts behind the theosophical movement — their brotherhood, their knowledge, and their aim of helping human evolution.
p: The Masters are perfected men, not spirits or gods
They form a brotherhood watching over human progress
The theosophical movement is their work

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: States the fundamentals: the unity of all life, the one universal law, cyclical evolution, and the septenary structure of cosmos and man.
p: All life is one; separateness is illusion
One universal law governs every plane
Evolution works in cycles and sevens

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Explains the doctrine of planetary chains and rounds — the earth as one globe in a septenary chain through which the human life-wave passes.
p: Each planet belongs to a chain of seven globes
The life-wave passes around the chain in seven rounds
Earth is the fourth globe of our chain — the densest

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Details the seven principles of man, from the physical body to the divine spirit, and their division into the mortal lower quaternary and immortal upper triad.
p: Seven principles: body, astral, prana, kama, manas, buddhi, atma
The lower four perish; the upper triad endures
Man mirrors the sevenfold cosmos

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Describes the physical body and its astral double — the subtle design-body that sustains the physical and survives it for a time after death.
p: The astral body is the subtle model of the physical
Prana, the life-force, animates the two
At death the astral double gradually disintegrates

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Analyses kama, the desire principle — the seat of passion and sensation — and its role in binding the soul to rebirth.
p: Kama is the principle of desire and emotion
It survives death as the kama-rupa or desire-body
Uncontrolled desire is the great binder to earth

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Treats manas, the mind principle — the thinker and reincarnating ego — and the division into lower (personal) and higher (spiritual) mind.
p: Manas is the thinker, the real man
Lower manas mixes with desire; higher manas aspires to buddhi
The destiny of the soul hinges on which way the mind turns

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Presents reincarnation as the method of evolution — the soul returning to earth life after life to learn, grow, and pay its karmic debts.
p: Rebirth is the schooling of the soul
Each life is a reaping of past sowing
Evolution requires many lives, not one

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Answers objections and details the process: the interval between lives, the conditions of the new birth, and the moral logic of the doctrine.
p: A devachanic interval separates incarnations
The new birth is fashioned by the karma of the old
The doctrine explains heredity’s puzzles better than chance

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Marshals the arguments: innate ideas, child genius, the justice of varied lots, the testimony of ages, and flashes of past-life memory.
p: Genius and innate character imply prior experience
Only rebirth makes life’s inequalities just
The doctrine is ancient and worldwide

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Expounds karma — the law of ethical causation — as the unfailing adjuster that weaves destiny from thought, word, and deed.
p: Karma is action and its inevitable reaction
Thought is the most potent karmic seed
Karma is not fate: new thought creates new destiny

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Describes kama-loka, the after-death realm of desire where the soul sheds its earthly passions before rising to devachan.
p: Kama-loka purges the lower desires
The kama-rupa or spook of the séance room belongs here
The process is nature’s, not a punishment

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Describes devachan, the blissful state of rest and assimilation between incarnations, where the soul dwells on the noblest experiences of the past life.
p: Devachan is a subjective heaven of the soul’s own making
Its length is proportioned to the life’s spiritual harvest
It is rest, not progress — progress needs earth

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Teaches the law of cycles in nature, history, and individual life — the returning tides that bring opportunities round again.
p: All growth moves in cycles and returning tides
History, nations, and souls obey cyclic law
Knowing one’s cycle lets one work with nature

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Applies theosophy to evolution: the inner, spiritual plan precedes outer form, explaining the missing links that baffle materialist biology.
p: Form follows an inner, pre-existing astral plan
Missing links reflect the descent of spirit into matter
Man’s form is far older than science supposed

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Surveys psychic phenomena — mesmerism, clairvoyance, apparitions — and the hidden forces behind them, with warnings against their pursuit.
p: Psychic powers are natural but latent faculties
Phenomena belong to the astral, the lowest subtle plane
Their pursuit without ethics is dangerous

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Examines spiritualism in the light of theosophy: séance “spirits” are mostly shells and elementals, and mediumship is injurious to the medium.
p: Genuine communications from the dead are rare
Most séance figures are astral shells animated by elementals
Mediumship drains vitality and invites obsession

title: The Ocean of Theosophy
author: William Q. Judge
s: Judge’s notes and references supporting the text.
p: Sources drawn from The Secret Doctrine and the Mahatma Letters

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: Title pages of Manly P. Hall’s encyclopedia of esoteric symbolism, first published in 1928.
p: A survey of the mystery-traditions of all ages
Famous for its many symbolic illustrations

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: Hall’s preface: the purpose of the work — to gather the scattered fragments of the ancient wisdom into one encyclopedic survey of symbolism and philosophy.
p: An encyclopedic survey of the mystery teachings
Symbolism is treated as the language of the sages
The work is offered to the serious student

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: The introduction defines the scope: the secret teachings preserved by the initiates of every age, and the method of reading them through symbols.
p: A secret tradition runs through all ages
Symbols are its universal language
The wise of every nation are its witnesses

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: The Ancient Mysteries and Secret Societies
s: On the ancient mysteries — Eleusis, Samothrace, and the rest — and the secret societies that carried the torch into later times.
p: The mysteries were the custodians of the doctrine
Initiation conferred both knowledge and obligation
Secret societies preserve the fragments today

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: Atlantis and the Gods of Antiquity
s: On Atlantis, its destruction, and the gods of antiquity as the deified teachers and heroes of the sunken world.
p: Atlantis is treated as a historical fact
The gods of antiquity are its remembered kings and teachers
Myth preserves the history of a lost continent

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: The Life and Teachings of Thoth Hermes Trismegistus
s: On Thoth-Hermes Trismegistus — the Egyptian father of the wisdom — his life, his books, and the Hermetic teaching.
p: Hermes is the reputed author of the Hermetica
The Emerald Tablet is the seed of alchemy
The Hermetic axiom: as above, so below

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the Great Pyramid as a temple of initiation — its chambers, its symbolism, and the rites enacted within.
p: The pyramid is read as an initiatory structure
Its chambers figure the stages of the path
Astronomy and geometry are built into its form

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: Isis, the Virgin of the World
s: On Isis — the virgin of the world, mother of the mysteries — and the meaning of her veil and her search for Osiris.
p: Isis is nature, the mother of all
Her veil covers the secrets of manifestation
The myth encodes the drama of the soul

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the sun as the universal deity of the ancient world — the solar myths and their esoteric meaning.
p: Sun-worship is the oldest religion
The solar year figures the cycle of initiation
The sun is the glyph of the logos

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the zodiac — the twelve signs as the alphabet of the heavens and the key to the astro-myths.
p: The zodiac is the book of the heavens
Its signs figure the stages of the soul’s year
Astro-theology underlies the scriptures

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the Bembine Table — the famous Egyptian tablet as a compendium of the mysteries.
p: The tablet is read as a syllabus of initiation
Its figures encode the theology of Egypt

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the wonders of the ancient world — oracles, sacred fires, and animated statues — and their occult explanation.
p: The wonders rested on real knowledge
Oracles used natural magnetic and psychic laws
Antiquity’s marvels are natural, not supernatural

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: The Life and Philosophy of Pythagoras
s: On Pythagoras — his life, his school at Crotona, and his philosophy of number and harmony.
p: Pythagoras taught number as the key to nature
His school was a mystery-community
Harmony of the spheres crowns his system

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On Pythagorean mathematics — the sacred decad, the tetractys, and the philosophy of numbers.
p: Number is the essence of things
The tetractys contains the decad and the cosmos
Mathematics is the first theology

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the human body in symbolism — man as the measure of the universe, the microcosm mirroring the macrocosm.
p: Man is the microcosm of the great world
The body’s members have cosmic correspondences
The temple is built in man’s image

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the Hiramic legend — the martyrdom of Hiram Abiff and its meaning in Masonic and universal symbolism.
p: Hiram’s death and raising figure the soul’s drama
The legend is the heart of Masonry
Its parallels run through all the mysteries

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: The Pythagorean Theory of Music and Color
s: On the harmony of music and color — the correspondence of tones and hues with the planets and the soul.
p: Music and color are one law in two octaves
The planets have their tones and colors
Harmony heals because it reflects the cosmos

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: Fishes, Insects, Animals, Reptiles and Birds
s: On the symbolism of the animal kingdom — the sacred animals, birds, reptiles, and insects of the myths.
p: Animals are hieroglyphs of qualities and powers
The serpent, the lion, the eagle recur worldwide
Totemism preserves the symbolic keys

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the symbolism of the vegetable kingdom — the world-tree, the sacred plants, and the fruit of knowledge.
p: The tree of life grows in every mythology
Sacred plants served the mysteries
The lotus and the rose are east and west of one symbol

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the symbolism of stones, metals, and gems — the mineral kingdom in alchemy and ritual.
p: Gems correspond to planets and virtues
The metals are the alphabet of alchemy
The philosopher’s stone is the crown of the mineral work

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On ceremonial magic and sorcery — the evocation of spirits, the grimoires, and the difference between theurgy and goetia.
p: Ceremonial magic is the ritual use of the hidden forces
Theurgy invokes the divine; goetia the infernal
The sorcerer is the magician inverted

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the four elements and their inhabitants — gnomes, undines, sylphs, and salamanders.
p: Each element has its own order of beings
The elementals are the forces of nature personified
Paracelsus is the chief authority

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On Hermetic medicine — the occult theory of disease and cure, spagyric remedies, and the medicine of the ancients.
p: Disease has an occult side
Spagyric medicine treats the whole man
The astral body is the key to health

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: The Qabbalah, the Secret Doctrine of Israel
s: On the Qabbalah — the secret doctrine of Israel, its books, and its place among the mysteries.
p: The Qabbalah is the Western tree of the doctrine
The Zohar is its greatest book
It preserves the keys of the Old Testament

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On Qabbalistic cosmogony — Ain Soph, the emanations, and the four worlds.
p: Ain Soph is the boundless
Emanation, not creation from nothing, is the doctrine
Four worlds descend from the crown

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the Tree of Life — the ten Sephiroth and the twenty-two paths, the glyph of God, universe, and man.
p: The Sephiroth are the divine emanations
The tree is a map of all planes
Man’s soul ascends the tree

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: Qabbalistic Keys to the Creation of Man
s: On the Qabbalistic keys to Genesis — Adam Kadmon, the fall, and the making of man.
p: Adam Kadmon is the heavenly man
The fall is the descent into matter
Genesis read by the key becomes cosmogony

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the Tarot — the twenty-two major arcana as the pictured pages of the secret doctrine.
p: The Tarot is a book in disguise
The arcana figure the soul’s journey
Its symbols unite number, letter, and image

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the Tabernacle — its construction as a cosmic diagram and the symbolism of its furniture.
p: The Tabernacle is a model of the universe
Its measures encode astronomical knowledge
The Ark is the throne of the presence

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: The Fraternity of the Rose Cross
s: On the Rosicrucians — their manifestos, their mysterious founder, and their mission in Europe.
p: The Fama and Confessio announced the fraternity
Christian Rosenkreutz is its legendary founder
The fraternity worked for the reformation of learning

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the Rosicrucian doctrines — the threefold world, the invisible college, and the rose upon the cross.
p: The rose on the cross is the soul unfolded on matter
The invisible college works unseen
Their tenets wed religion, philosophy, and science

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: An analysis of fifteen famous Rosicrucian and Qabbalistic diagrams.
p: The diagrams are compendia of the doctrine
Each is a meditation in symbolic form

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On alchemy and its great exponents — from the Arabs to Paracelsus and the European adepts.
p: Alchemy is both a chemistry and a religion
Its masters are traced through the centuries
The gold sought was first of all within

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: The Theory and Practice of Alchemy
s: On the theory and practice of alchemy — the great work, its stages, and its materials.
p: The great work proceeds by solve et coagula
Its stages are marked by colors
The prima materia is the commonest and most despised thing

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: The Hermetic And Alchemical Figures of Claudius De Dominico Celentano Vallis Novi
s: An analysis of the Hermetic and alchemical figures of Vallis Novi’s manuscript.
p: The figures are a symbolic laboratory
They veil the operations of the great work

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the Chymical Wedding of Christian Rosenkreutz — the alchemical romance as an initiatory allegory.
p: The Chemical Wedding is an initiatory drama
Its seven days figure the stages of the work
The marriage is the union of soul and spirit

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On Bacon, Shakespeare, and the Rosicrucians — the cipher theories and the hidden authorship question.
p: Hall examines the Baconian cipher claims
The plays are read as vehicles of the secret teaching
The question is left to the evidence

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
chapter: The Cryptogram as a factor in Symbolic Philosophy
s: On cryptograms — ciphers and secret writing as instruments of the hidden teaching.
p: Cipher has served the secret societies
Biliteral and other systems are explained
Books themselves may be cryptograms

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On Masonic symbolism — the tools, the degrees, and the temple as the house of the soul.
p: Masonry is the heir of the mysteries
Its working tools are moral symbols
The temple is man himself

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On mystic Christianity — the esoteric meaning of the Christos, the virgin birth, and the inner life of the Christian mysteries.
p: The Christos is the divine principle in man
The gospel story is an initiatory drama
Mystic Christianity unites the churches at the root

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the cross and the crucifixion — the world-symbol of spirit bound to matter.
p: The cross is older than Christianity
It figures the descent of spirit into matter
The crucifixion is the mystery of incarnation

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the Apocalypse — the Book of Revelation read as an initiatory text.
p: Revelation is a book of symbols, not of dates
Its drama is the regeneration of the world and the soul
The seals and trumpets mark the stages

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On Islam — its teaching, its mystics, and its place among the world-religions.
p: Islam’s unitary faith is presented sympathetically
Sufism is its mystical heart
The Koran has its esoteric reading

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the symbolism of the American Indians — the sun dance, the medicine wheel, and the mound-builders.
p: The native traditions preserve archaic symbols
The wheel and the dance figure the cosmic order
America has its own mystery-heritage

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: On the emissaries of the mysteries — the adepts and teachers sent into the world age after age.
p: The great teachers are links in one chain
Each age receives the messenger it can bear
The work never ceases

title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
s: Hall’s conclusion — the unity of the secret teachings and the call to the student to seek the light.
p: All the traditions are one at the summit
The student is bidden to seek and to serve
The book ends where the path begins

title: The Shape of Things to Come
author: H. G. Wells
chapter: Book the First: Today and Tomorrow — The Age of Frustration Dawns
s: Book One of Wells’ future-history: the state of the world after the Great War, and the dawning recognition that the old order cannot continue.
p: Written as a history of the future, framed as Dr. Raven’s dream book
The old order of sovereign states is failing
A new world order struggles to be born

title: The Shape of Things to Come
author: H. G. Wells
s: A chronological note on the dating and framework of the narrative.
p: Sets the time-scheme of the future history

title: The Shape of Things to Come
author: H. G. Wells
chapter: Early Attempts to Understand and Deal with These Disproportions
s: Early attempts to understand and correct the disproportions — the criticisms of Karl Marx and Henry George.
p: Marx and George are examined as early diagnosticians
Their partial truths and errors are weighed
The problem outlasted their solutions

title: The Shape of Things to Come
author: H. G. Wells
chapter: The Way in Which Competition and Monetary Inefficiency Strained the Old Order
s: On how competition and monetary inefficiency strained the old order to breaking.
p: Monetary breakdown was a chief agent of collapse
Competition without plan became waste

title: The Voice of the Silence
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Blavatsky introduces this translation of three fragments from the Book of the Golden Precepts, a mystical work studied by her Eastern teachers, and explains that the verses guide the disciple from the life of the senses toward the “Voice of the Silence” — the inner divine Self.
p: The fragments come from the Book of the Golden Precepts, memorized by her teachers
The work is addressed to disciples seeking the Path
The “Voice of the Silence” is the voice of the higher Self within

title: The Voice of the Silence
author: H. P. Blavatsky
chapter: Fragment I. The Voice of the Silence
s: The first fragment teaches the stilling of the senses and mind so the inner voice may be heard. It contrasts the fleeting personality with the eternal individuality and describes the early stages of interior awakening.
p: The mind must become still before the inner voice can be heard
The personality is transient; the individuality endures
Shamballa and the sacred land are named as spiritual guardians of the teaching

title: The Voice of the Silence
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: This fragment presents the two paths open to the aspirant: the open path of liberation-for-self and the secret path of renunciation, where the liberated one remains to help humanity. It urges compassion as the soul of the Path.
p: Two paths: the “open” path to nirvana and the “secret” path of self-sacrifice
Compassion is the supreme law of the Path
The Bodhisattva ideal: renouncing nirvana to serve mankind

title: The Voice of the Silence
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: The final fragment describes seven portals — the paramitas and mystical stages — through which the candidate must pass, culminating in the crossing of the great waters and the attainment of the “other shore”.
p: Seven portals correspond to the transcendent virtues (paramitas)
Each gate tests the candidate’s purity, courage, and detachment
The goal is Prajna — direct wisdom — and crossing to the “other shore”

title: The Voice of the Silence
author: H. P. Blavatsky
s: Blavatsky’s notes explaining Sanskrit and Tibetan terms, schools, and doctrines referenced in the verses.
p: Definitions of key Buddhist and esoteric terms
References to the Arhat, Bodhisattva, and Dhyani traditions

title: Thought-Forms
author: Besant & Leadbeater
s: On the difficulty of representing subtler forms in physical colour — the necessary imperfection of the plates.
p: Astral forms exceed physical colour in brilliance
The plates are approximations, not photographs
The reader must allow for the medium’s limits

title: Thought-Forms
author: Besant & Leadbeater
s: The two effects of every thought: the radiating vibration and the floating form — the wave and the shape that thought produces.
p: Every thought sends out a vibration
Every thought also builds a form
The two effects act on different principles

title: Thought-Forms
author: Besant & Leadbeater
s: On the form and its effect — the thought-form as a temporary living entity, its size, persistence, and working.
p: The thought-form is a temporary living entity
Strong thought builds clear, enduring forms
The form works toward the end its maker intended

title: Thought-Forms
author: Besant & Leadbeater
s: The key to the colours — what each hue of the astral and mental bodies signifies, from the black of malice to the pale blue of devotion.
p: Colour is the language of the subtler matter
Anger is red, devotion blue, intellect yellow, love rose
Clear colours mark pure feeling; muddy colours, selfish

title: Thought-Forms
author: Besant & Leadbeater
s: The three classes of thought-forms — those that take the thinker’s image, those that picture material objects, and those that take a form of their own.
p: Class one: the image of the thinker
Class two: the image of the object thought of
Class three: forms proper to the thought’s own nature

title: Thought-Forms
author: Besant & Leadbeater
s: The gallery of illustrative thought-forms — affection, devotion, intellect, ambition, anger, sympathy, fear, and greed pictured as they appear to the seer.
p: Each emotion has its characteristic form and colour
The plates give actual observed examples
Sudden fright, sustained anger, grasping greed are all portrayed

title: Thought-Forms
author: Besant & Leadbeater
s: Forms built by music — the splendid mountains of form raised by the music of Mendelssohn, Gounod, and Wagner above the church where they were played.
p: Music builds vast forms above the place where it sounds
Each composer has his characteristic form and colour
Sound is a builder on the subtler planes

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
s: Master E.K. opens by presenting astrology as the subjective lamp of a living being — the science that illumines the timing and quality of life from within.
p: Astrology is called the subjective lamp of a living being
It reveals when our good seeds sprout and when obstructions come
Its use is guidance for right action, not fatalism

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
s: The scriptural basis of astrology — how the ancient scriptures of the world presuppose and teach the science of the heavens.
p: The scriptures of all nations contain astrology
The science descends from the most ancient teachers
Scriptural stories veil astronomical and spiritual truths

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
s: The Vedic tradition of astrology — its antiquity, its unbroken line, and its foundation in the wisdom of the heavens.
p: Vedic astrology is an unbroken ancient tradition
It treats the heavens as a living order
Its purpose is the welfare of the being, not prediction alone

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
s: On worlds within worlds — the seed-principle: as the banyan seed contains the tree, each world contains subtler worlds within it.
p: Every seed contains its kingdom
The subtle worlds enfold the gross
Man is a world containing worlds

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
s: On the validity of the zodiac — the word means a group of living animals, and the zodiac is the living belt of cosmic intelligences.
p: The zodiac is a living group, not a dead diagram
Its signs are qualities of cosmic life
Its validity rests on the correspondence of man and cosmos

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
chapter: The Measures of Time in the Zodiac
s: On the measures of time hidden in the zodiac — the zodiac symbolizing both space and time.
p: The zodiac measures time as well as space
The great ages are read from its wheel
Time and space are two faces of one order

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
s: On the clock in space — how man discovered the measurement of time by watching the heavens.
p: The heavens are the first clock
The discovery of time-keeping came from watching the sky
The cosmic order is reflected in our instruments

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
s: On the nature of time — why beings rise at different hours, and how time conditions all manifestation.
p: Time conditions every form of life
Each being has its own hours of rhythm
To know time is to cooperate with nature

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
s: On the influence of the planets — the Indian tradition’s unbroken testimony to the planetary governance of life.
p: The planets influence life by a real law
The Indian tradition has preserved this knowledge unbroken
Influence is invitation, not compulsion

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
chapter: The Principles Governed by the Planets
s: On the principles of man governed by the planets — the whole solar system understood as one unit reflected in the human constitution.
p: The solar system is one unit of life
Each planet corresponds to a principle in man
Man is the microcosm of the solar order

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
s: On the planets and their colours — the correspondences of hue and planetary ray.
p: Each planet has its colour
The correspondences differ among authors; the tradition is explained
Colour is the garment of the planetary quality

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
chapter: Planets and the Hours of the Day
s: On the planets and the hours of the day — the planetary rulership of the hours from sunrise.
p: The hours of day and night are ruled in sequence by the planets
The first hour at sunrise gives the day its ruler
The order of the planetary hours explains the week

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
chapter: Division of Work According to the Planets in the Seven Days
s: On dividing work according to the planets of the seven days — the practical weekly rhythm of the tradition.
p: Each day carries its planet’s quality
Work harmonized with the day prospers
The week is a spiritual calendar

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
s: On the Moon in the Vedic tradition — the lunar principles and the three principles to be understood for reading the heavens.
p: The Moon holds a central place in Vedic astrology
Lunar mansions measure the month
The Moon governs the mind and the waters

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
s: On the astrological tradition itself — its history as valuable as the science, and the line of its teachers.
p: The history of a science is part of the science
The tradition descends through the sages
Reverence for the line keeps the teaching pure

title: Wisdom of the Heavens
author: Master E.K. (Kulapati E. Krishnamacharya)
s: On cataclysms and astrology — the balance of the elements and the cosmic timings of great changes.
p: Balance of the elements means birth of harmony; imbalance, cataclysm
Great changes have their cosmic timings
Astrology reads the approach of the turning-points
